From your first variable to calling an API, in five sections. Each section has a **lesson** to read and an **exercises** page: try on your own first, open a hint if you are stuck, then compare with the solution.

Each section comes with a zip of the notebooks and the data, so you can run everything on your computer (Python 3 with Jupyter, or [Anaconda](https://www.anaconda.com/download)).

1. **[Python basics](01-python-basics.ipynb)**: Types, operators, strings, data structures, conditions, loops and functions. [Exercises →](01-python-basics-exercises.ipynb)
2. **[NumPy and pandas](02-numpy-pandas.ipynb)**: Arrays with NumPy, then loading, cleaning, combining and reshaping tables with pandas. [Exercises →](02-numpy-pandas-exercises.ipynb)
3. **[Data visualisation](03-data-visualization.ipynb)**: Exploring a dataset with Plotly Express: distributions, comparisons, relationships. [Exercises →](03-data-visualization-exercises.ipynb)
4. **[Interactive charts](04-interactive-charts.ipynb)**: Subplots, sliders, dropdowns and animations with plotly.graph_objects. [Exercises →](04-interactive-charts-exercises.ipynb)
5. **[Working with APIs](05-apis.ipynb)**: What an API is, and how to call one from Python with requests. [Exercises →](05-apis-exercises.ipynb)
